grading: Correct requires every requested material fact, no contradictions or unsupported guess; partial omissions/unresolved; incorrect material contradiction. Grade each answer independently.

answers.expected_answer: Twelve ordinary turns: four seasons, each three ordinary rounds then a courtship. No player turn, rotation, monument reputation or Servants’ Hall use on courtship; only courtship resolves.

Rotate service; resolve round event then ongoing effects; choose activity; invite exact required gentry; provide service; enjoy favours; optional market buy; clear board. Used servants to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, tile upgraded if needed and returned to correct tableau column; last player advances marker.

All servants directly Available; all personal discard gentry to hand; round event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or free market refresh; optional one tile purchase; last player advances marker. Hiring on pass is expansion/optional and excluded here.

Legal if four needed servants are in Servants’ Quarters and costs payable. Service Help costs 3 increments each, Quarters to Available only. Screening reputation fixed after step 2 before step 3 is level 6 for tile and guests all turn; later loss does not invalidate.

All positive before all negative. Cannot take loss first at minimum; ignore only loss beyond minimum after positives. Must pay money penalty; activity income, VP money or Borrow Money can fund it. If unable to fund full payment cannot play guest.

Borrow £100 costs 2 increments, repeatable; Service Help 3 increments per servant Quarters to Available, repeatable; Refresh Market 4 increments, special action once per turn. Need enough reputation; no specials at minimum 1.1. No direct refresh from Expended via Service Help.

Use available butler/underbutler, no gentry. Take up to two from Servants for Hire except underbutler to Expended Service; used butler also expended and tile upgrades. Upgraded room may instead recruit one common footman/valet/lady’s maid from anywhere on one opponent board to your Expended, never unique servants.
Housekeeper only no available lady’s maid; footman requires Brushing Room and no available valet. Underbutler may replace butler/valet/footman even if regular available.

Only acquire Butler’s Pantry; gain underbutler from supply immediately into Expended Service. Cannot hire with Butler’s Room or hire-servant VP card; unique, cannot be recruited. He is not immediately available: normally Expended to Quarters at the next service rotation, then Available at the second subsequent rotation. A pass or Refresh Service VP card can make him available sooner; once in Quarters, Service Help or the Quarters tile can allow earlier use.
Market space price plus tile modifier; Reserve £300 plus modifier; minimum £100. Cannot acquire duplicates by any means. May purchase above reputation; PR restricts play only.

Slide remaining left; stack drawn duplicate on match and draw again; qualifying Service/PR1 drawn tile to Reserve and draw again; sort new tiles by ascending sorting number when filling multiple spaces. One remaining duplicate keeps space occupied so no refill.

After season1 all Service except Largest Wine Cellar; after season2 PR1. Later eligible draws go straight Reserve. Full Market refresh after first three courtships standard under compendium/corrigendum; old stable-market aid incomplete.

Return both Fairchilds first. Total current theme-category tile VP including negatives; highest draws VP and chooses one Fairchild to hand. Ties all draw VP and no Fairchild. Each discards one objective face down; shuffle together and bottom objective deck. At season setup first player passes anticlockwise.

Sum tile VP in all four revealed theme categories, repeated categories count repeatedly/double for two. Highest wins Fairchild+VP; tied highest reputation level breaks tie ignoring wheel position; if still tied no Fairchild, tied winners draw VP. After courtship final special actions and VP-card benefits if possible, then scoring.

Tiles including negative; gentry in hand/discard incl final Fairchild and negatives; remaining objectives; reputation 1,3,6,10,15,21,28 for levels1–7; servants2 each; £200 per1VP rounded down; unused VP cards. Tie: final Fairchild holder, then highest rep level ignoring position, then shared victory.

5 setup+2 Draw Objectives=7; discard1 each of4 courtships leaves3. Shuffle simultaneous face-down discards before bottom deck. Extra objective effects increase final total by1 each. Tile objectives require possession at end, no upgrade required.

Immediately on draw or anytime own turn; final chance after final courtship. Reveal and discard to bottom VP deck for benefit; may use several. Retain hidden with objectives and score printed VP if not discarded; no both benefit and VP.

First use normal tile flips to upgrade at cleanup, mandatory; upgraded stays. Hybrid flips each use and moves correct category, starts underlined hybrid icon side. Activity-to-monument flips after first use and never hosts again. Only currently face-up hybrid category counts.

After event in step2 hosting or step3 pass. Monuments1rep per ordinary turn, no courtship. Hall any one available servant on tile to lower opponent1 gain1; used servant expended end turn; still host activity/pass. Cannot target minimum-rep opponent.

Heritage one casual from hand, footman tile and guest normal service; double all favours including negative, stays upgraded activity. Queen one prestige from hand, housekeeper tile and normal guest service; double1 chosen favour others normal; upgrades monument. Lionheart butler tile draws1 prestige from deck no guest service, double all nonnegative favours, keep guest to discard; upgrades monument. All fixed1 cannot modify count.

Choose the first player randomly. Family selection begins to that player’s left and proceeds clockwise. Asquith gets the extra Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets an extra footman in Available Service.

Use 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters, with 1 showing and marker at position 1; exclude 7/8. Five Available servants: butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, footman. Five starter-side-up tiles: Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green. Four family cards: Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady; Asquith additionally gets Dowager. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300).
source_refs: pp.8–10; lines 314–348,361–364; PDF p.9 starter tile images

answers.expected_answer: Three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen and two underbutlers. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants return to the box and are unavailable this game.

Separate and shuffle the starter guests and deal two per player. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starters are casual guests distinguished by an icon, with no other special properties.

Five double-sided monuments for four players, with at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite enter as activity tiles, are always included, and do not count against this monument selection. Include all other nonstarter base tiles; return unused starters and unselected double-sided monuments to the box.

Six different occupied spaces: PR3 or lower (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them after filling; stack duplicates in one space. Normal upgrade icon hidden; hybrid underlined icon up. Sort ascending tile sorting number beginning at £300. None of the named PR4/Hall/monument cases is eligible.

Standard sixteen-space side, marker at 1; one reminder token per player; both Fairchild cards face up on Alderley Hall. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme. Keep earlier themes face up and put each new one to their right; all four count at final courtship.
Each servant moves only one space: Expended to Quarters; Quarters to Available. Move Quarters first to avoid accidentally moving an expended servant twice. Unused Available servants remain Available.

No immediate reward: the round event occurs before the activity, so the Study is unupgraded when the event is checked. An already-upgraded Study grants £300 and two reputation. Standard Village Fair spaces are 3 and 9.
source_refs: pp.17,99; lines 650–676,3754–3755; PDF p.12 standard track

answers.expected_answer: Resolve before ongoing tile effects in step 2 hosting or step 3 passing. Standard space 6 draws two objectives and keeps both hidden. Passing players also receive this event.
Yes, ignore all tile and guest PR during this hosting activity; still obey exact gentry numbers/types and every required service. It grants no extra hosting activity when passing. Standard space 14.

Buy any affordable number from Market and/or Reserve at existing prices in a single unchanged Market. No sliding/refilling after individual purchases and no refreshing after the first Holiday purchase. Finish buying, then refill all empty spaces together. Market Purchase VP card works like Builders’ Holiday.

Set all Market tiles aside. Refill all six Market spaces under normal rules, including sorting new tiles, before returning removed tiles to the bag and mixing. Do not touch Reserve tiles. Removed tiles cannot recur in that same refresh.

Each symbol moves one wheel position: 5 to 1 raises a level; 1 to 5 lowers it. Standard minimum 1.1 and maximum 7.5. Ignore loss beyond minimum. Use special actions before or during a favour to create space; immediately spend excess on specials or lose it. All special-action payments must be affordable.
Money held is public. No giving or receiving money between players in this mode. Never spend more than held. Supply is unlimited; use proxies when coins run out. Denomination exchange is allowed.

Female family members can fulfil ladies requirements. Family cannot fulfil casual-guest requirements. Use exactly the required number and types, with no extra attendees. Family has no PR or personal service; tile service and PR still apply.

Ordinary invite draws from indicated deck, reveals the new guest to all and adds it to hand. Screening draws the stated number and keeps the stated number: reveal only the kept cards, adding them to hand. Rejected cards are hidden and go to the bottom of the appropriate guest deck.

Dismissal is optional. You may dismiss a guest just drawn earlier, or from hand, current activity or personal discard, but never family. Put it on the bottom of its guest deck. It is no longer owned and neither returns on passing nor scores for you.
Lord gains £200. Lady chooses screening two casual guests and keeping one, OR optionally dismissing one guest. Heir chooses £100 OR one reputation. Asquith Dowager gains both £100 AND one reputation.

Only a male prestige guest triggers the bonus: Charles qualifies; male casual and female prestige guests do not. Gain two reputation in addition to the Young Lady’s normal casual-guest draw. Charles is prestige despite having no PR.

Both are prestige guests with no PR. Charles requires a valet and gives three reputation. Elizabeth requires a lady’s maid and gives both one prestige-guest draw and two reputation. They are guests, not family, so family dismissal immunity does not apply. Return Fairchilds to Alderley Hall at each courtship.

Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Oliver reduces one opponent by two and loses one reputation herself. Neither card grants its owner reputation as Hall does. A player at minimum 1.1 cannot be targeted; apply general positive-before-negative and minimum-floor rules.
Gain one reputation each time an Estate activity is hosted. Mere Estate ownership and passing do not trigger it; use the activity tile’s current category.

The tile permits using one servant from Quarters each turn in addition to Available servants, without Service Help’s three-reputation cost. Ordinary rotation still occurs first. A servant used this way goes to Expended Service at turn end.

Front requires butler and two family, with no tile favour; then mandatory upgrade. Upgraded side is ongoing-only, cannot host again, and pays £300 and two reputation only at Village Fair, not every turn.

Unupgraded: butler and two family draw one objective. Upgraded: butler and three family draw one VP card. The extra objective increases the final retained total by one, without increasing courtship discards.
Draw two objectives and keep one; put the other on the bottom of the objective deck. The retained card increases final scoring objectives by one, not an exchange or additional discard.
Yes: all servants move directly to Available Service and can be used immediately. Service Help costs three reputation per one servant and only moves Quarters to Available, not directly from Expended.
Take one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot immediately provide service without a separate refresh effect.
Return any one gentry card, including family, from personal discard to hand. It can be used immediately and attend this activity if it meets its requirements.

The base basic-servant objective gives one VP per common footman, valet or lady’s maid, excluding butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Normal service VP counts every servant at two VP each; the ten-servant objective counts all servants in employ and gives seven VP.

The monument objective gives three VP per monument, including upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite. Category objectives give one VP per tile in that category, including monuments and hybrids; only the final face-up hybrid category counts. Queen’s Suite is Estate; Lionheart is Prestige.

Nature Group: eleven VP for Flower Room plus any one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden or Garden Maze. Domestic Group: twelve VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. End-game possession suffices; use/upgrade is unnecessary.

Prestige objective gives one VP per prestige guest, including final Fairchild. The other gives one VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests, casual and prestige, including final Fairchild. Family never counts; incomplete groups do not score.

The reputation objective gives seven VP for maximum level 7 (Max counter), independent of wheel position, as clarified by the official French publisher base-rulebook objective example. Wealth objective gives ten VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP or reputation tie resolution.
source_refs: Official French publisher base rulebook (Super Meeple), PDF pp.7 and14; objective example explicitly maximum reputation level, identified by Max counter; see supplemental-source-provenance.json.

answers.expected_answer: Both sides require a butler and three family. Front draws one prestige guest. Upgraded side draws one prestige guest and optionally dismisses one to four guests from hand, activity or discard to the bottom of their decks. It remains an activity, unlike the excluded alternate ongoing version.
There is no limit to either hand or personal discard size. Discarded gentry still belong to you, may be recovered by passing and count for your final gentry VP.
All Reserve tiles are public and may be inspected at any time; choose any eligible tile to buy, not only the top tile. Normal price, uniqueness, affordability and purchase limits still apply.

Passing is a voluntary turn choice even when an activity is possible. If a preferred activity cannot meet all requirements, choose another legal activity or pass. If no activity can be hosted, you must pass.

Yes, subject to the normal timing and available resources/cards. The once-per-turn limit is only on the paid special action. The pass refresh and each VP-card refresh are separate methods and do not consume that special-action allowance. One pass grants only one passing benefit.
